title: Standardize variant-semver mapping and automated changelog scaffold for model onboarding
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: onboarding currently uses informal "variants" (e.g. "fp16", "int8-q4", "q4_0-k") with no stable, machine-readable version stamp. This leads to ambiguity when producing release notes, migrating profiles, and routing fallbacks. This PR introduces an explicit variant->semver mapping and a changelog scaffolding flow that automates release note snippets for model profile deltas.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a canonical mapping module (registry/variant_semver.py) that maps variant identifiers to a 3-segment semver-like stamp: major.variant.minor (e.g. 3.fp16.1 -> "3.0.1-fp16" internally). The mapping is intentionally human-readable while enabling deterministic sorting and compatibility checks.
- Adds a pre-release hook (tools/changelog_scaffold.py) that consumes profile diffs produced by the onboard CLI and emits a structured release note draft under releases/autogenerated/<model>-<semver>.md. The scaffold extracts: changed profile fields (latency/cost/regression flags), quantization notes, and suggested consumer-facing bullets.
- Adds a migration script (scripts/migrate_existing_variants.sh) to stamp existing models with a generated semver and append alias metadata for backward-compatible lookups.
- Updates onboarding CLI (cli/onboard.py) to validate variant-semver alignment and to optionally emit a changelog fragment when --scaffold-changelog is passed.
- Adds unit tests and integration fixtures for the mapping behavior and changelog output.

Implementation notes:
- Variant semver design choice: we avoid embedding hardware SKU or cloud-region into the stamp; the stamp is model+variant-focused so routing policies remain orthogonal. Compatibility rules are encoded as simple semver comparison helper functions (registry/compat.py) used by rollout and fallback policies.
- Changelog scaffolding intentionally avoids auto-publishing: it writes a draft markdown and raises a Linear comment with the suggested body if --linear-key is supplied. This keeps release authors in the loop.
- The mapping module exposes a stable API for other subsystems (console, release assembler, routing) to call and resolve canonical variant tags.

Testing & validation performed:
- Unit: registry variant mapping edge cases (dash/underscore normalizations, numeric suffix bumps)
- Integration: onboard CLI end-to-end with a small model fixture; scaffold output validated against the release snippet schema
- CI: forced e2e regen of sample performance profiles to ensure no accidental profile drift. The e2e job was flaky on the first run (timing-related), retried and passed.

Migration plan:
1) Merge this PR to main behind a short maintenance window.
2) Run scripts/migrate_existing_variants.sh in staging to generate stamped metadata for all models in model-registry and push draft release notes into releases/autogenerated.
3) Run a 24-hour compatibility sweep: use registry/compat.py to verify that current routing rules can resolve to the new stamped variants; fallback heuristics are exercised in the canary environment.
4) Roll the change to prod and monitor the consoles/alerts for increased 404s on model variants (none expected).

Rollback: rollback simply reverts the stamped fields and removes the autogenerated drafts. The scaffold does not publish notes automatically, so no risk of leaking partial release notes.

Checklist (x = done):
[x] variant_semver module + helpers
[x] changelog_scaffold script + tests
[x] CLI integration (+ flag)
[x] migration script and one-time run docs
[x] unit + integration tests

Related: ENG-1219 (onboard semver requirements), ENG-1302 (release automation follow-ups), SUP-4821 (support ticket referencing variant ambiguity), internal design doc: doc/design/variant-semver.md

Notes for reviewers: please focus on registry/compat.py semantics and the choices in the mapping normalization function (we prefer stable, deterministic outputs even if they look slightly verbose). The migration script is idempotent and logs a dry-run by default.
